In [[mathematics]], a '''torsion sheaf''' is a [[sheaf (mathematics)|sheaf]] of abelian groups <math>\mathcal{F}</math> on a [[Grothendieck_topology#Sites_and_sheaves|site]] for which, for every object ''U'', the space of sections <math>\Gamma(U, \mathcal{F})</math> is a [[torsion group|torsion abelian group]]. Similarly, for a [[prime number]] ''p'', we say a sheaf <math>\mathcal{F}</math> is '''''p''-torsion''' if every section over any object is killed by a power of&nbsp;''p''.

A torsion sheaf on an étale site is the union of its [[constructible sheaf|constructible subsheaves]].<ref>{{harvnb|Milne|2012|loc=Remark 17.6}}</ref>
